Compounded on the default engine by a read that never loaded the bitmaps: `modelsdk/gen` declares all four as `string` while Mendix stores BSON **binary**, so `DecodeString` returned `""` for every real icon — the same gen/storage mismatch class as scheduled events and regular expressions
insight: **Silence is preservation, not removal** — an absent clause must carry the stored value, so removing needs its own syntax (`NOT EXPOSED`, `DROP ICON`). Rebuilding a sub-document from the subset MDL can express is the general shape of this bug (ADR-0005); look for `X = &T{...}` where `X` is a stored polymorphic child. **Check the READ before blaming the write**: a merge cannot carry what the reader never loaded, and a gen accessor typed `string` over a BSON binary fails silently to `""`. **Two microflow renderers exist** in `cmd_microflows_show.go` (`describeMicroflow` and `renderMicroflowMDL`) — patching one leaves DESCRIBE unchanged on the path the CLI actually takes. A test fixture generating two same-sized PNGs produces **identical bytes**, so an "each target is routed separately" assertion passes vacuously unless the fixtures differ

symptom: `alter settings` writes a microflow, entity or constant name that does not exist, reports success, and `mxcli check --references` calls the script valid — the build then fails with **CE1613** *"The selected microflow/constant no longer exists"*. A misspelled constant is worse than a dangling pointer: the override is **created** for a constant that does not exist, leaving dead configuration data
cause: Settings were the ONLY statement family that resolved nothing. `--references` walks `validateWithContext`, whose switch had no `*ast.AlterSettingsStmt` case at all, so the qualified names in `AfterStartupMicroflow` / `BeforeShutdownMicroflow` / `HealthCheckMicroflow`, workflow `UserEntity` and the constant override went straight to the writer
file: `mdl/executor/validate_settings_refs.go` (`validateSettingsReferences`, `validateSettingsConstantRef`), wired into `mdl/executor/validate.go` (the `AlterSettingsStmt` case + `scriptContext.constants`) and into `alterSettings` itself; index helper `buildConstantQualifiedNames` in `mdl/executor/helpers.go`
insight: Put the guard in the **handler**, and have check call the same functions — that is what makes `exec` refuse exactly what `check` reports, including under `--no-check`, and it is why the exec-time call passes a **nil script context**: by then the earlier statements have run, so anything the script created is really in the project. Three cases a naive resolver gets wrong, each with a test: an **empty value clears** the setting (Studio Pro's "(none)") and must not be resolved; a document **created earlier in the same script** is not missing (the escape hatch every other family has, which is why the fixture pair is a `.fail.mdl` AND a passing control); and **dropping** a constant override must stay legal even when the constant is gone, or there is no way to tidy up after deleting one. Note the two `ValidateProgram`s are different passes — the package-level one (which `exec` runs) has only a project PATH, while the reference pass has a connected backend, so a check needing project reads cannot live in the first. Repro `mdl-examples/bug-tests/274-settings-reference-validation.fail.mdl` + `274-settings-reference-valid.mdl`. Issue #274

symptom: A decision inside `while` is written with only its **true** flow — Studio Pro reports **CE0079** *"the 'false' condition value should be configured on an outgoing sequence flow"*. `mxcli check` reports "Syntax OK" and exit 0, so the broken microflow is written by `exec` and surfaces only in the Errors pane. The same body inside `loop` is correct
cause: A merge-less split (`if X then break` / `then continue`) defers its FALSE case to the next flow. `addLoopStatement` tracks that deferred case through the body and wires whatever is left over to a synthesized `ContinueEvent` (ledger #52); `addWhileStatement` had **neither** the `pendingCase` variable nor the trailing block, so the case was dropped. Four shapes affected: break-last, continue-last, either with a trailing statement, either after a leading statement
insight: Mirror `addLoopStatement` **verbatim** — a WHILE body is a loop body, and the divergence was the whole defect. The durable guard is the **parity test**: assert LOOP and WHILE agree on the same body, which is what would have caught the ledger #52 fix landing in only one of two builders. Grep for the sibling before fixing any loop-body defect. Note `return`-in-a-loop is refused by MDL062, so `break` and `continue` are the only live shapes. Not expressible as a `.fail.mdl`: the MDL is **valid** and `check` is right to accept it (this is a writer defect, not a check gap), so the guards are unit tests in `mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_while_break_test.go`. Repro `mdl-examples/bug-tests/893-while-break-false-edge.mdl`. Issue #893 case 3 — note the reported shape (`IF` first in a WHILE body) did **not** reproduce; this was found by probing its neighbourhood, and cases 1/2/6 were already fixed by MDL061/062/063

symptom: `describe microflow` renders a loop with an **empty body** — `loop $X in $L begin end loop;` — when the body carries an `@annotation`. Silent, exit 0, and the truncated script passes `check`, so the documented describe → exec round trip **deletes the loop body**. `bson dump` and `--format mermaid` both still show the activity
cause: `emitLoopBody` picks the body's start as "no incoming sequence flow, leftmost then topmost" (`preferLoopBodyStart`). A `*microflows.Annotation` **is** an object in `ObjectCollection.Objects` but connects via `AnnotationFlows`, never `Flows`, so its incoming count is permanently 0 and it was always a start candidate. When it won, traversal began at a node with no outgoing sequence flow and emitted nothing. Only loops: the top level starts from its `StartEvent`, and mermaid iterates objects directly rather than traversing
insight: **The defect is positional, and that is the trap**: annotation LEFT / ABOVE-same-X / ABOVE-LEFT lose the body, annotation RIGHT renders correctly *including* the annotation — so a fixture that puts it on the right passes against broken code. Cover all four. **Not Studio Pro-only**, which was the first wrong reading: mxcli's own builder emits the annotation at the same X and above (measured activity (150,80), annotation (150,-20)), the losing shape, so mxcli destroyed loop bodies it authored itself. **Why #330 missed it**: that fixture covers the same construct, but its Go regression tests the AST→BSON *build* path and its describe assertion is a manual procedure in a comment — `make check-mdl` runs without a project, so CI only syntax-checked it. Nothing had ever *described* an annotated loop body. The durable guard is a **build → describe round trip** using the builder's real positions, asserting its own premise so it fails loudly if layout changes stop it exercising the defect. Not expressible as `.fail.mdl` (the MDL is valid; the bug was in describe). Repro `mdl-examples/bug-tests/965-loop-body-lost-to-annotation.mdl`, guards `mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_describe_loop_annotation_test.go`. Issue #965

symptom: `create association … comment 'text'` reports success and stores **no documentation**, and a `/** … */` doc comment before the statement is dropped too — so an association is the one domain-model element with no working way to document it on create. `mx check` passes (an undocumented association is valid), and `describe association` simply shows nothing
cause: Both halves sit upstream of the writer, which has emitted `Documentation` all along. (1) `mdl/visitor/visitor_association.go` never called `findDocCommentText(ctx)`, the way the entity and enumeration visitors do, so `stmt.Documentation` was always empty. (2) The **plain-CREATE** branches of `execCreateAssociation` built the `Association` / `CrossModuleAssociation` literal without a `Documentation` field at all — while the `OR MODIFY` branches a few lines above them *do* set it, which is what makes the field look wired when the file is read casually
file: `mdl/executor/cmd_associations.go` (`associationDocumentation`, both plain-CREATE literals, both OR MODIFY branches), `mdl/visitor/visitor_association.go`; tests `mdl/executor/cmd_associations_documentation_test.go`
insight: **A field set on the OR MODIFY path is not evidence it is set on the CREATE path** — the two construct the element separately and sit next to each other. Grep for the struct literal, not for the field name. This is also why `comment` was *kept* on `create association` when it was removed from entity/enumeration/module/microflow/nanoflow/rule: there the doc comment already worked so the dead option was redundant, but here **neither** spelling worked, and removing the option would have left nothing at all. Check both spellings before deciding whether an option is dead or load-bearing

raw: | Every member of an **array-rooted** import/export mapping is rejected: `"id" is not a member of the JSON structure at (Object), which has no members there` — while the identical body over an object-rooted structure works | Both executors hardcoded the root lookup to `"(Object)"`, and an array-rooted structure is built at `"(Array)"` with its item at `"(Array)|(Object)"` (`buildElementFromRawRootArray`). The root resolved to nothing, so the child lookup reported members "at (Object)" — a node that structure never had, which reads as "your key is wrong" rather than "the root was looked up in the wrong place". 122 of the 327 mapping documents in the demo apps are array-rooted, the single largest gap in the mapping surface | `mdl/executor/cmd_import_mappings.go` (`buildImportMappingElementModel`, `jsonSchemaIndex.root`), `mdl/executor/cmd_export_mappings.go` (`buildExportMappingElementModel`, `buildExportRootArrayElement`, `exportRootToPrint`) | Take the root FROM the structure instead of assuming it. No new syntax: the structure decides, and Studio Pro does not ask either. The import side then needs nothing more — the array branch was already stepping `"(Array)"` → `"(Array)|(Object)"` for NESTED arrays. **The two sides store different shapes and the difference is not guessable**: an array-rooted IMPORT mapping is ONE element at `(Array)|(Object)` (the container collapses), an array-rooted EXPORT mapping is a bare `Array` container at `(Array)` whose single child carries the entity with `ObjectHandling=Parameter`. Pin both against Studio Pro documents before writing either (`Teamcenter.IMM_ItemRevision`, `FactoryManagement.IMM_ScenarioList`, `SnowflakeIntegration.EXM_SensorData` — Evora demo app, 11.13). A second export shape exists (`DigitalTwin.EMM_EntityQuery`: entity on the container, `Find` on the item, for a parameter that OWNS the list) and MDL cannot say which is meant, so it stays unauthorable — #262. **Adding an authorable shape means teaching DESCRIBE about it in the same change**, or the newly writable mapping joins the 112 silent-loss cases of #260: the export container is not `Kind=="Object"`, so it fell into the value branch and printed `Root = ` with its whole subtree dropped. Discriminate the container on its stored **JsonPath**, not on `Kind` — the two engines' readers label it differently ("Array" vs "Object") and only the path is in the document. Controls: revert the root lookup and the repro returns verbatim, while the object-rooted control still passes; `mdl-examples/bug-tests/519-rest-mapping-as-list-of.mdl` goes from dying on its own mapping statement to executing. `mx check` needs the base project's own error count as the control (a blank app carries a pre-existing CE0495). Repro `mdl-examples/bug-tests/248-array-rooted-mappings.mdl`, tests `TestImportMappingArrayRoot` / `TestExportMappingArrayRoot`. Issue #248 |

The document is `MessageDefinitions$MessageDefinitionCollection` — a COLLECTION, which is why the reference is three parts (`Module.Collection.Definition`) — and it is derived from the **domain model**, not a payload sample: every node names an entity or an attribute and carries two names, its own (`Emails`) and the singular one its items take (`Email`) | `mdl/executor/mapping_messagedefinition.go` (`findMessageDefinition`, `messageDefPaths`, the two builders), `mdl/backend/modelsdk/messagedefinition_read.go`, `model/types.go` (`MessageDefinitionCollection`, and `XmlPath` on both mapping element types) | **A message-definition mapping stores BOTH path families** — that is the whole reason it needs its own builder rather than a branch of the JSON one: `json=(Array)\|(Object)\|From` beside `xml=Emails\|Email\|From`. cause: `TestMappingFixtureRoundTrip`'s `knownLossy` is a version-blind expectation, but the document it is asserted against is not always version-stable. `loadMappingFixture` uses the **base project's own copy** whenever the blank app already ships a document of that name (FeedbackModule ships two), instead of the pinned `.bson` — and that copy changes with the Mendix version. `FeedbackModule.IMM_PostResponse` loses exactly one property, `MessageDefinition2`, which `modelsdk/gen/mappings/version.go` records as `Introduced: "11.10.0"`, so below 11.10 there is nothing to drop and the staleness guard fires
file: `mdl/executor/mapping_fixture_roundtrip_test.go` (`knownLossyFrom`, and the base-project log line in `loadMappingFixture`)
insight: Gate the entry with `knownLossyFrom` — `ProjectVersion().IsAtLeast(major, minor)` — rather than deleting it, or the real defect (#279) stops being caught on the versions that have it. **Only ONE of the two FeedbackModule mappings failed, and that asymmetry is the diagnosis**: the export twin also loses #277's `IsKey`/`MaxLength` and #279's `MinOccurs`, which exist on every version, so it stays lossy throughout — if both had failed, the cause would have been something else. Check a suspect property against `gen`'s `version.go` `Introduced` before theorising. The substitution that makes this possible is now **logged** ("using the BASE PROJECT's copy"); it was silent, which is what made a one-line cause cost a nightly. To reproduce another version locally: `mxcli setup mxbuild --version 11.6.0` then `MX_BINARY=~/.mxcli/mxbuild/11.6.0/modeler/mx go test -tags integration ./mdl/executor/`. Prove it in both directions — disable the gate and watch the nightly failure reappear on 11.6

symptom: `DESCRIBE LAYOUT` prints a header and no widget structure at all, for a document with 84 elements. Nothing distinguishes it from a genuinely empty layout
cause: `getLayoutWidgetsFromRaw` read `rawData["Widget"]`, a key `Forms$Layout` does not have. Its tree hangs off `Content` — a `Forms$WebLayoutContent` (or `Forms$NativeLayoutContent`) whose `Widgets` array holds the root. The type assertion failed and returned nil, silently
insight: **A `ScrollContainer` holds its regions in five named slots — `Top`, `Right`, `Bottom`, `Left`, `CenterRegion`** (the last spelled unlike its siblings), not in a list. The walk read `CenterRegion` alone, which was survivable for pages and wrong for layouts: the topbar is in `Top` and the navigation in `Left`, so the two things anyone describes a layout to see were the two it skipped. Each occupied slot is now a synthetic region node, the same way `TabControl` preserves tab pages. Controlled by restoring each half separately. ako/mxcli-ledger #136

symptom: A bulk `ALTER PAGES … SET LAYOUT` reports success and the build then fails with **CE1613** "The selected placeholder … no longer exists", naming a page rather than the statement
cause: The repoint rewrote `Form` and every `Parameter` without checking that the target layout declares the placeholders the page binds to, so a page bound to `HeaderLeft` got `NewLayout.HeaderLeft` pointing at nothing
insight: **Check after MAP is applied** — `MAP (Old AS New)` exists precisely to rebind onto a placeholder the new layout does have, so checking before it would refuse the remedy. A target that reports *no* placeholders is one the backend could not read (MCP exposes none), not one that has none, so it skips rather than refusing everything. And **name the remedy in syntax that parses**: the grammar is `MAP (Old AS New)`, while the comment beside the rule had said `MAP (Main -> Main)` since it was written — the arrow reads plausibly and is a parse error

symptom: A caption/title/content written from MDL shows as the empty-caption placeholder (`<>`) in Studio Pro, with a "no translation for this language" warning, on a project whose language is not en_US. `mxcli`, `mx check` and mxbuild all report success
cause: Mendix has no language-neutral text — every `Texts$Translation` carries a `LanguageCode` — and every executor CREATION site hardcoded `"en_US"`, ignoring the project's `DefaultLanguageCode`. The read side had already been fixed for the same reason (#702, `describeDefaultLanguage`); the write side was never wired to it
insight: **Resolve the write language from the project, never a literal.** `DefaultLanguageCode` is by definition enabled, so this cannot produce the unenabled-language case #257 warns about, and DESCRIBE reads the same language CREATE writes so describe→exec round-trips on a non-en_US project. **Two layers, two different seams.** The executor sites build a `model.Text` and can reach `ctx` — fix those first, they are the reported bug. The writer leaves (`sdk/mpr`, `modelsdk`, `widgetobj`, `pagemutator`, `modelsdk/mpr`) build a `Texts$Text` from a **bare Go string** and have no context: a widget `Label`, a pluggable column caption, a navigation item and a menu-document item all land there. **Do not thread a parameter to them** — measured, that is 183 function signatures across five packages (113 in `sdk/mpr` alone), nearly every widget writer, to carry a value constant for the whole run. They read `model.AuthoringLanguage()` instead, published once by `describeDefaultLanguage`. `ALTER PAGE … SET Caption` was never affected: it edits the stored translation in place and keeps its `LanguageCode`. The control that localises it is free: Studio Pro's own pages in the same project store the same word under the right language — and beware counting those as mxcli's, scope the search to the unit. `mx check` reports 0 errors before AND after, so it proves nothing here; assert on the stored `LanguageCode`. mendixlabs/mxcli#970

symptom: Replaying a `create or replace snippet` silently resets its translated captions to the source language in every language. The run says `Created snippet` (on a document that already exists), `mx check` reports 0 errors, and the app renders in one language
cause: The snippet replace path was an unconditional **delete-then-create**. Nothing `canon.Reconcile` does survives that: by the time the create runs there is no stored document left to transplant identities from or to compare against, so translations — and anything else MDL cannot express — go with the deleted unit
file: `mdl/executor/cmd_pages_create_v3.go` (`execCreateSnippetV3`); the correct pattern is 40 lines above it in `execCreatePageV3`
insight: **A replace must be an UPDATE on the stored unit's ID, never delete+create.** Reuse `snippetsToDelete[0]` as the new document's ID, call `UpdateSnippet` (which already existed and was called nowhere), and delete only the *extra* duplicates. The verb is the tell: a path that prints `Created` on a replace is not going through the write choke point, so it gets neither the identity transplant nor the unchanged-elision. **The control is free and in the same run** — put a page and a snippet with the same shape in one script and replay it: before the fix the page reports `Unchanged` and keeps its Dutch while the snippet reports `Created` and loses it, which is what makes it a snippet defect rather than a fact about replacing documents. Second consequence the page path already documents: delete+add churns git and crashes Studio Pro's RevStatusCache. ako/mxcli-ledger #143

symptom: A mapping names a schema source that does not exist and mxcli writes it through — mxbuild reports it as **CE1613** "… no longer exists" at build time, while `mxcli check` and even `check --references` pass; and the same typo silently switches off EVERY member check in that mapping
cause: The schema index is empty whenever the structure cannot be loaded FOR ANY REASON, and `resolvable()` reads an empty index as "there is nothing to validate against" (its correct meaning for a schema-less mapping). So `with json structure M.NoSuchThing { create M.Loc { LocId = nonsense } }` had two errors and reported neither. Separately `null values` was written as free text, so `null values Banana` reached the stored NullValueOption verbatim — the enum is {LeaveOutElement, SendAsNil}
insight: **Refuse at the SOURCE, do not make `resolvable()` stricter**: a NAMED but unresolvable source is an error, while NO source at all — XML schema, message definition, schema-less test mappings — must keep working, and conflating the two breaks every one of them. **An empty project and a backend that cannot LIST look identical from here**, so the refusal only fires when the listing succeeds; a listing error takes the name at face value. That distinction has teeth: two pre-existing mock tests named a structure their mock did not provide and started failing, and the right fix was to give the mock the structure rather than weaken the check — a mapping whose named source does not exist is an inconsistent model to assert against. Name what would have worked, the shape #882 established for members. **Still written through**: `with xml schema M.NoSuchThing`. A gen type exists (`modelsdk/gen/xmlschemas`) so it is verifiable, but it needs a new `ListXmlSchemas` across the interface, both engines and the mock; the silent-disabling half does not apply there, since an XML mapping never had member validation at all. Repro `mdl-examples/bug-tests/mapping-259-resolve-schema-sources.mdl`, tests `mdl/executor/mapping_source_resolution_test.go`. Issue ako/mxcli#259

symptom: Pages that were valid start failing **CE6206** "Attribute paths with multiple steps cannot be used on pages that are accessible through an offline-based navigation" — and nothing in the script that wrote them changed
cause: An offline navigation profile restricts every page it can reach to at most ONE association hop. Adding the PROFILE is what invalidates pages written earlier, so the error appears far from its cause. mxcli writes multi-step paths happily: a datagrid column bound `Req_Asset/Asset_Site/SiteName` stores an `IndirectEntityRef` with two steps and `mx check` reports 0 errors — correctly, until an offline profile exists
insight: **The threshold is two hops, not one** — pinned by a control inside the reference page, which carried both and had only the 2-step one flagged (`MaintenanceRequest_Asset → AssetName` accepted, `… → Asset_Site → SiteName` rejected). In MDL a hop is a slash, so the count is `strings.Count(path, "/")` and no BSON walk is needed. Two traps: an **XPath constraint** is also full of slashes and is NOT an attribute path, so scan attribute bindings only; and a dynamic text binds through **template parameters** rather than `Attribute:`, which is how the second reported error was written. The rule deliberately does NOT decide reachability — Studio Pro walks the whole page graph and `check` does not build the catalog — so it warns naming the profile rather than asserting an error it cannot prove. ako/mxcli-maintenance §6/§7 screenshots

symptom: `create or replace navigation Phone` fails with `navigation profile not found: Phone (available: Responsive)`, and no other mxcli command adds one — so a device-specific front end cannot be built from MDL. A layout naming the missing profile then fails **CE1613**
cause: `CREATE OR REPLACE NAVIGATION` only ever REPLACED a stored profile. Mendix routes a phone to a Phone **profile** on the User-Agent, not on viewport width, so the profile is the thing that makes phone pages reachable
file: `mdl/executor/cmd_navigation.go` (creates when the name is a known kind), `mdl/backend/modelsdk/navigation_profile_add.go` (`newWebProfileBson`), `mdl/types/navigation_profile_kind.go` (the closed set)
insight: **Measure what Studio Pro CREATES, not what the reference project HAS.** All six web profiles store the same 14 keys and differ only in Kind and Name — offline profiles included, so there is one builder, not two. The trap is `ProgressiveWebAppSettings`: the reference app's Phone and TabletOffline profiles both carry `{Precaching: true, InstallPrompt: true}`, and a first draft copied that. Those are the USER'S settings — the schema defaults `Precaching` to false, makes the element optional, and a profile added through Studio Pro's own model API stores **null** for every kind. `mx check` reports 0 errors either way, so the only way to tell is to ADD a profile over PED (`ped_update_document`, add to `/profiles`) and read back what it materialised — reading an existing profile measures the user, not the platform. The kind set is **closed**: creating `Phone` adds what the platform routes to, creating `Mobile` would add one that never can, so an unknown name stays an error; Hybrid and native kinds are excluded for want of a reference. The kind table lives in `mdl/types` because both the executor and the backend need it and the executor must not import a backend implementation (ADR-0002). ako/mxcli-maintenance §7

symptom: `grant <Role> on System.User (...)` fails with `load domain model 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002: open …/mprcontents/00/00/….mxunit: no such file or directory`, which reads like a corrupt project
cause: The System module's domain model is **not a stored unit** in any Mendix project — mxcli synthesises it from a built-in table so System entities can be REFERENCED. The write reached storage, missed the unit, and surfaced as a filesystem error
insight: **Refuse by name up front, not by letting the write fail.** A late failure also leaves half-applied state — the roles have already been validated by then. Say in the message that this is true of every Mendix project, or the reader goes hunting for corruption that is not there. Worth stating the consequence too: an XPath constraint that TRAVERSES System is equally unusable, so filtering `Administration.Account` by `[System.UserRoles/System.UserRole/Name = ...]` returns nothing — target a user ROLE and record who acted, which is what the maintenance app did. The guard must be case-insensitive on the module name and must not catch a module merely CONTAINING "System"; there is a control test. ako/mxcli-maintenance §4

symptom: An import mapping with `find` / `find or create` is accepted by `mxcli check` AND by `exec` ("Created import mapping"), and the project is then unbuildable: **CE0250** "Object element must have a key defined if object handling is set to 'Search for an object'" and/or **CE0251** "Searching for an object is not allowed for the entity 'X', because it is not persistable"
cause: Neither requirement was checked anywhere. `def.ObjectHandling` was carried to `elem.ObjectHandling` unconditionally, `elem.IsKey` was set nearby but never cross-checked against the handling, and the entity's persistability was not consulted at all. The failure lands a build later, so an agent generating MDL gets no signal at the point it can still fix the statement
file: `mdl/executor/validate_import_mapping_find.go` (`MDL-MAP02` key, `MDL-MAP03` persistable), wired from `validate_program.go` so BOTH `check` and `exec` run it
insight: **mxbuild reports ONE AT A TIME** — a keyless `find` over a non-persistent entity is CE0250 *only*, and CE0251 appears only once a key exists, so fixing the key half looks like it fixed everything until someone adds a key. **Persistability follows the GENERALIZATION CHAIN, not the entity's own flag**: `create entity Sub extends NpBase` stores `Persistable: true` (mxcli's own catalog reads it as PERSISTENT) and mxbuild still says CE0251 — a rule reading the flag misses exactly that case, and the control (`Sub extends Keeper`, persistable parent) must stay silent. Both errors are raised **per object element**, not only at the root ("at Object mapping element 'Pet'"). A **custom handler is exempt from both** — the executor stores ObjectHandling "Custom" whatever keyword was written, and 70 of the demo corpus's 88 `find` elements are that shape, so missing the exemption flags most real mappings. Resolve fail-OPEN: an entity that is in neither the script nor the project is *unknown*, never assumed non-persistable. Sweep control: describing all 151 corpus import mappings and re-checking gives 0 flags, and stripping the `key` markers from that same output gives 18 — a sweep that only shows zero proves nothing (an earlier run's "0" was a concatenated file that never parsed). ako/mxcli#253

symptom: `create entity X extends <parent>` passes `mxcli check --references` with "All references valid" whatever the parent is, then the build reports **CE1613** "The selected entity 'X' no longer exists" — or, if the parent was written unqualified, `mx check` dies with **System.AggregateException … 'Generalization' property** and validates nothing at all
cause: An entity's EXTENDS target was never collected as a reference. The generalization is stored BY NAME and written verbatim, so mxcli had no opinion about whether it resolved
insight: **The two failures are different sizes and want different gates.** A qualified-but-missing name is recoverable (the project loads, the build reports it) and needs the project to detect, so it belongs in the reference check. An UNQUALIFIED name makes the .mpr unopenable — same shape as #973's bare attribute name — and is a static property of the statement, so it is also MDL069 (fires with no project, which is what makes a `.fail.mdl` catchable by `make check-mdl`) and an executor guard at the TOP of `execCreateEntity`, before the module is auto-created, so `exec --no-check` cannot write it and a statement that can never be valid leaves nothing behind. **Resolve against the whole script, not the statements before it**: a generalization is resolved lazily and `create entity A extends B; create entity B;` is correct — `eagerDefRefs` says so explicitly, and a per-statement executor guard would break it, which is why only the syntactic half runs there. Controls worth keeping: a forward reference, `System.Image`, and an entity from a marketplace module must all still pass.

symptom: `DROP ENUMERATION Mod.Name` reports "enumeration not found" for one that `SHOW ENUMERATIONS`, `DESCRIBE ENUMERATION` and `ALTER ENUMERATION` all resolve in the same session
cause: The enumeration is inside a FOLDER, so its `ContainerID` is the folder's ID rather than the module's. DROP resolved the owning module with `findModuleByID`, which matches module IDs only, and the failed lookup `continue`d — dropping the candidate silently, so the match list came out empty
file: `mdl/executor/cmd_enumerations.go` (`execDropEnumeration`); the trap was `mdl/executor/helpers.go` (`findModuleByID`, now removed — DROP was its only caller)
insight: Resolve a container through `getHierarchy(ctx)` + `h.FindModuleID` + `h.GetModuleName`, which is what the other three commands already did — **never compare a `ContainerID` against the module list**, because it is only a module ID for an element at the module root. The helper that invited the mistake is gone rather than left for the next caller. Two controls belong in the fixture: an identical enumeration at the module ROOT (it passed before the fix, so it proves this is container resolution rather than "drop is broken") and one whose container walks to no module at all (must still be skipped, not dropped under a guessed name). Test-fixture trap met while writing it: an element created with the folder as its container has `ContainerID == folderID`, so registering `withContainer(h, enum.ContainerID, folderID)` writes folder → folder and hides the module behind a self-loop; register the FOLDER's parent only.

symptom: A `validation feedback $Var/Attr` on an INHERITED attribute builds as **CE1613** "The selected attribute 'Mod.Child.Attr' no longer exists", while `mxcli check --references` passes and DESCRIBE renders the statement back unchanged
cause: Mendix qualifies a member reference against the entity that DECLARES it, so an inherited attribute carries the ancestor's name. The builder used `fb.varTypes[variable]` — the variable's declared type — with no generalization walk. Both engines
insight: Same rule as #758 (access rules) and #703 (mappings), unlearned one layer over — when a member reference is built anywhere, ask whether it needs the DECLARING entity. **Do not reuse `ResolveMemberRef` for this**: its walk stops at `System.User` because a user entity's platform members must not appear in an ACCESS RULE (CE0066), which says nothing about referring to one from a microflow — reusing it falls back to the child's name, the exact bug being fixed. `DeclaringMemberRef` is the full-chain walk; the two stops are different questions and are kept apart deliberately. Controls that must be in the fixture: an attribute the entity declares ITSELF (a walk returning an ancestor for everything passes the inherited cases and is just as wrong), and the no-backend path, which keeps the naive spelling rather than emptying the reference.

symptom: A list widget over `$currentObject/Mod.Assoc` builds as **CE1613** "The selected attribute 'Mod.<WrongEnd>.Attr' no longer exists" — the rows are typed as the association's other end — when the page's context object is a SPECIALIZATION of one end. `mxcli check --references` passes
cause: `resolveAssociationDestination` picks the end opposite the context by comparing qualified names with `==`. A specialization equals neither end, both ends resolve so neither empty-end fallback applies, and control reaches `return childEntity` under the comment "default to the child (TO) side, which matches the common FROM=context pattern"
insight: **A comment saying "the common pattern" is a guess, and a guess that is silent when wrong is the bug.** Walk the generalization chain before falling through — over the domain models `pb` has ALREADY loaded, the same list the ends are resolved against, so the two cannot disagree about what an entity is (going through the backend would be a second source of truth for the same question). Apply it only when BOTH ends resolved: when one is empty the existing fallbacks are load-bearing (issuetracker #14) and a destination of "" makes the .mpr unloadable. The cross-association branch has the same `==` and needs the same treatment. Controls, ideally on one page: the context being the end ITSELF (reverse) and forward navigation from the other end — both passed before the fix, which is what makes this "the context is a specialization" rather than "reverse navigation is broken".

symptom: A microflow's `create` / `retrieve` / `create list of` naming an entity WITHOUT a module prefix passes `mxcli check --references` with "All references valid", then `mx check` fails to LOAD the project — `The text 'Name' is not a valid AttributeIdentifier` — so nothing else is reported either
cause: The reference collector skipped any entity reference whose `Module` was empty, and the builder writes the property only when both Module and Name are set. So an unqualified name was neither validated nor written: `create` stores no `Entity` key at all (its member assignments then reach disk as bare words) and `retrieve` stores the equally invalid `".Thing"`
file: `mdl/executor/validate_microflow.go` (`checkQualifiedEntityRef`, MDL008 — the rule that already covered PARAMETERS), plus the guards in `validate.go` (`refs.entities`) and `cmd_microflows_builder_actions.go` that let it through
insight: **This is upstream #973 and the reported trigger is not the cause** — omitting `$X =` reproduces nothing on either engine; the entity is stored correctly. Chase the *reported symptom* ("Entity reference remains empty") rather than the reported *cause*. Control that separates the two: a QUALIFIED name that resolves to nothing was always caught (`entity not found: … (referenced by create)`), so it is the absent prefix, not the absent entity, that opened the hole. Prefer a project-less lint rule over a reference-check entry for this class: it is a static property of the statement, so it also fires with no `-p`, gates `exec`, and makes a `.fail.mdl` that CI can actually run. Related trap found alongside: DESCRIBE prints `$NewObject = create …` for an activity whose output variable is empty — a name invented at format time (`cmd_microflows_format_action.go`), so reading a document back through describe cannot tell you whether the variable is set.

symptom: A task-page button "does nothing": the microflow runs, no error is shown, and the runtime log has `Client: You can't complete this user task, it is not assigned to you`. `mxcli check`, `mx check` and the build are all clean
cause: `SET TASK OUTCOME` was called on a user task nobody had claimed. `TARGETING XPATH` / `TARGETING MICROFLOW` decides who may SEE a task — it does NOT assign it, and there is no `ASSIGN TASK` statement
file: `mdl/executor/validate_task_claim.go` (`ValidateTaskClaims`, MDL-WORKFLOW10), wired from `validate_program.go`; the platform rule is in `.claude/skills/mendix/write-workflows/SKILL.md`
insight: Claiming is a plain write to the Assignees association and must come BEFORE the outcome: `change $Task (System.WorkflowUserTask_Assignees = [%CurrentUser%]); commit $Task; set task outcome …`. Two things the rule needs: walk the body **in order** (a claim written after the outcome does not help, so collecting all claims first would pass it), and match the association on its **member name** — it parses qualified, bare and quoted, and matching one spelling would warn about correct code. A WARNING, never an error: the task may be claimed in a microflow this one calls, so accept a claim inside a branch rather than trying to evaluate the condition. Related trap: `WorkflowUserTask.Name` holds the task CAPTION, not the activity name, so an inbox routed on the activity name silently never matches. ako/mxcli-maintenance-2

symptom: A `CALL WORKFLOW` whose parameter mapping is written across two lines builds to **CE0109** `"Undefined variable 'Request\n  '"`. The identical call on ONE line is fine, and `CALL MICROFLOW` is fine at any width
cause: The workflow context is stored as a variable NAME, but it is filled from an expression SOURCE — and the visitor deliberately preserves an expression's trailing whitespace so a multi-line expression round-trips byte-for-byte (`appendExpressionListTrailingWhitespace`)
insight: **Trim the NAME, not the expression.** The obvious fix — a `TrimSpace` in the visitor — breaks the round-trip the whitespace exists for, and there are tests pinning it (`TestRetrieveRangeExpressionsPreserveTrailingWhitespace` and friends). The asymmetry between CALL WORKFLOW and CALL MICROFLOW **is the diagnosis**: microflow arguments stay expressions, where trailing whitespace is harmless, so anywhere an expression source is used as a NAME is the place to look. Trim BEFORE stripping the leading `$`. The control must assert the exact string — the name looks correct in most output until printed with `%q`. ako/mxcli-maintenance-2

symptom: A page builds to **CE1571** "No argument has been selected for parameter 'X' and no default is available" while `mxcli check --references` passes — the microflow data source was written as `datasource: microflow M.F` with no arguments
cause: Nothing compared the flow's SIGNATURE against the data source's arguments. The microflow itself resolves, so the reference check was satisfied and the fault only surfaced at the far end of an `mx check`
file: `mdl/executor/validate_datasource_args.go` (`validateDataSourceArguments`, `dataSourceArgErrors`, `buildFlowParameterNames`), wired from `mdl/executor/validate.go` for both pages and snippets; `scriptContext.flowParams`
insight: **An ERROR, not a warning, and the measurement is what licenses that**: a page with NO parameters and a page WITH a `$Task` parameter of the microflow parameter's exact entity type BOTH get CE1571, so Studio Pro does not auto-map an object in scope and a missing argument is never filled in. Mendix's own wording ("no default is available") suggests otherwise — measure before trusting it. Three controls the rule needs or it is worse than nothing: a **parameterless** microflow with no parens must stay clean (the common case — flagging it would get the rule turned off), an **unresolvable** flow must be left to `validateWidgetReferences` (else a typo'd flow NAME is reported as a missing ARGUMENT, pointing at the wrong line), and the **correct** form must pass. Record script-defined flow signatures in `scriptContext.flowParams` the way `javaActions` already does, or the check only ever fires on a flow that already existed — one script creating a data source microflow and the page that binds it is the common shape. Verified both ways against mxbuild: the flagged widget is exactly the one CE1571 names, and the corrected example builds at 0 errors. ako/mxcli-maintenance-2

symptom: `create user role Administrator (...)` fails with `user role already exists`, and since `exec` halts on the first error every later statement in the security script is skipped — leading to the conclusion that `CREATE OR MODIFY USER ROLE` does not exist
cause: It does exist and is re-runnable; it requires the parenthesised module-role list, so `create or modify user role Administrator;` fails with `mismatched input ';' expecting '('` — which reads as "unsupported verb" rather than "missing argument"
insight: **Name the re-runnable form in the error.** A blank Mendix app already ships an `Administrator` user role, so this fires on the first realistic security script. Before adding "missing" MDL surface from a field report, run the statement — this one was filed as a missing feature and was a discoverability failure. ako/mxcli-maintenance-2

symptom: `ContentParams: [{1} = $PageVar]` comes back from DESCRIBE as `<unbound>`
cause: TWO different faults wearing one symptom. On the DEFAULT engine the write is CORRECT — the stored parameter carries `SourceVariable { LocalVariable: "Name" }` — and the READER looked only at `SourceVariable.PageParameter`, found no `AttributeRef` beside it, and fell through to `<unbound>`. On the LEGACY engine the write really was wrong: it put every binding in `PageParameter`, ignoring the kind
insight: **Read the stored bytes before believing "silently dropped"** — half of this report was the tool disagreeing with itself, not with Mendix, and re-executing the describe output is what would have made it true. Studio Pro populates exactly one of `LocalVariable` / `PageParameter` / `SnippetParameter` on the same `Forms$PageVariable`; a local variable renders bare (`$Name`), the other two carry an `AttributeRef` and render `$Name.Attr`. **Two describers for one stored shape is the actual defect** — the pluggable one already read all three and the other did not, so they now share one resolver rather than being fixed twice.

symptom: A page variable declared `Enumeration(Mod.Enum)` is stored and described as `String`; a variable typed `Unknown` reverts to `String` on the next page rewrite
cause: Two silent defaults, stacked. `mdlTypeToBsonType` had no enumeration case and returned `DataTypes$ObjectType` for anything unrecognised; `localVarTypeToGen` then had no ObjectType case and returned a `StringType`. A type nobody had mapped came out as "String", twice, without a word
insight: The qualified name was in the AST all along — the visitor keeps the data type's raw SOURCE TEXT, so `Enumeration(Mod.Status)` arrives complete and only needed parsing; look there before adding a field. A `DataTypes$EnumerationType` needs its `Enumeration` by-name key or Mendix resolves it to null, so an enumeration with no qualified name is deliberately NOT written as one. Fix all four corners together — builder, both writers, and DESCRIBE — or the round trip loses the type at whichever end was missed; `Unchanged page …` on a describe → exec is the proof that reader and writer agree. Stacked defaults are the pattern to look for here: each one is individually defensible and together they erase information.

symptom: `describe page` emits MDL that mxcli's OWN `check --references` rejects — `duplicate widget name 'row1' … (CE0495)` — on stock pages nobody edited
cause: The names are DERIVED at describe time and Mendix stores none of them: `Forms$LayoutGridRow` and `Forms$LayoutGridColumn` carry no `Name` key, and a DataGrid2 column's name is derived from its bound attribute (mxcli says so itself in MDL-WIDGET16). Rows and columns restart numbering per grid, and two columns over one attribute derive one name — so the check was citing a Mendix error for something Mendix does not check
insight: **Ask whether the model even HAS the name before enforcing uniqueness on it** — dump the stored widget and look for the `Name` key. A name mxcli invented cannot be a duplicate of anything. This one is also worth remembering for how the triage was WRONG: the first read predicted describe should renumber and called exempting them "the weaker choice"; measuring reversed it twice, because there is no stored name to make unique AND `ALTER PAGE` already handles a repeated derived column name ("column %q is ambiguous … qualify the reference as `ON gridName.%s`"), so renaming would have broken documented addressing to fix a non-collision. The control is mandatory here: two widgets Mendix DOES name, sharing a name, must still be reported, or the change reads as "stop checking for duplicates".

raw: | A literal tab typed into an MDL string reaches the model as the two characters `\t`, so a tab-delimited export becomes one cell per row and the failure looks like a Java bug. A literal NEWLINE in the same string survives, which makes the asymmetry easy to miss | `quoteExpressionLiteral` escaped `\n`/`\r`/`\t` before writing the **Mendix expression**, applying MDL's escaping rules to a different grammar. Mendix's expression engine has exactly one escape — an apostrophe is doubled — and no backslash escapes at all, so the stored `'a\tb'` IS a backslash and a `t`. The newline survived for an unrelated reason: a multi-line expression is kept as raw SOURCE text (`ast.SourceExpr`) and never reaches the escaping | `mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_helpers.go` (`quoteExpressionLiteral`, `expressionToString`) | **Measure the value where it lands, not where it is written.** Proven end to end against a running 11.13 runtime, straight out of Postgres: before, `length 4, 61 5c 74 62` (`a \ t b`); after, `length 3, 61 09 62` (a real tab). The escaping had a *documented rationale* that was simply false — "STRING_LITERAL does not accept them raw" — when the rule is `'\'' ( ~['\\] \| '\\' . \| '\'\'' )* '\''` and `~['\\]` admits every byte but an apostrophe and a backslash. **Read the grammar rather than the comment about it.** Round-trip is the thing to control: assert describe → exec reproduces the same stored bytes, and use the real parser (`visitor.Build`) rather than a hand-mirrored decoder — the old test asserted "output contains no control bytes", which was asserting the bug. A backslash followed by n/r/t is still doubled and still wrong for the same reason (3 stored chars where 2 were meant); it is load-bearing because describe emits the stored expression verbatim, so removing it needs describe to escape on output. Measured blast radius: 0 backslash escapes in any string value across 33,645 units in 90 projects. ako/mxcli-captrack #5 |

symptom: An attribute or entity named `Month` / `Year` / `Quarter` / `Day` passes `check --references`, then a view entity added weeks later fails **CE0174** ("The 'Month' part is incomplete or incorrect")
cause: An **OQL** reserved word, used **unquoted**. Three grammars stack and each treats quoting differently: MDL parser keywords (quoting works), Mendix platform reserved words (MDL021/CE7247, quoting does *not* — the check strips them), and Mendix **OQL** keywords (quoting **does** work — double quotes, as in SQL)
file: `mdl/executor/validate_oql_reserved_names.go` (MDL071, at CREATE/ALTER ADD/RENAME); `mdl/executor/oql_type_inference.go` (MDL032, inside a view's OQL)
insight: **Read the CE0174 text before concluding a name is unusable — it lists `OPEN_QUOTE` among what the parser expects.** Measured on 11.13.0: `select s."Month" as MonthNo` and `from Module."Year" as s` both build at **0 errors**, and mxcli passes the quotes through unchanged, so the fix is normally a quote in the view, not a rename. The one place quoting is unavailable is an **alias**, and that limit is **OQL's own**: it takes a bare identifier there for *any* name (`as "Total"`, reserved nowhere, is CE0174 too — reported as MDL072), so a view entity's own attribute (whose name IS its select alias) must be renamed. Hence MDL071 is a warning at the point the name is chosen, not an error. **This entry has corrected itself twice, both times by finally reading the error text.** First it asserted OQL had no quoted-identifier form (disproved by `OPEN_QUOTE` in the CE0174 message, and by the source report's own narrative: `SELECT "Year" FROM …` works). Then it asserted the alias limit was MDL's grammar rather than OQL's (disproved by `as "Total"` — reserved nowhere — also failing CE0174). The two CE0174 texts differ precisely in whether `OPEN_QUOTE` is listed; that difference is the whole answer and was present in the output from the first measurement onwards. Also: adding a warning to `ValidateEntity` surfaced a pre-existing trap — the exec guard was `if len(vs) > 0 { fail(vs[0]) }`, so every warning blocked the write and MDL022 had been doing so since it shipped. Use `firstBlockingViolation`, never the count; control that an MDL021 error still blocks and is not shadowed. ako/mxcli-captrack #1

symptom: `mxcli check` passes and `exec` prints `Created association`, then the project no longer OPENS — `KeyNotFoundException … at StreamingBsonUnitReader.ResolvePostponedProperties()`, a stack trace naming no document
cause: An association whose FROM entity lives in ANOTHER module. Mendix stores an association in the module of its FROM entity, so a remote FROM writes a `ParentPointer` aimed at an element in a different unit. Not a build error — a LOAD error, so Studio Pro cannot open it either
insight: **Refuse; there is nothing to write instead.** Neither stored form can express it: `DomainModels$Association` holds two element IDs both local to the unit, and `DomainModels$CrossAssociation` holds a local `ParentPointer` plus a BY_NAME `ChildRef` — there is no by-name PARENT. Check the storage shape before treating a direction as a writer bug. The reported case was `from System.User`, but it is **not System-specific** — `from Administration.Account` fails identically, and a guard keyed on System would pass the general case through; the rule is the module boundary. Control both ways: the supported direction (`from MyModule.X to System.User`) and a plain same-module association must stay at 0 errors, and stubbing the guard must bring the KeyNotFoundException back. To locate a dangling GUID at all, scan every `.mxunit` for the raw 16 bytes in BOTH endiannesses (`uuid.bytes` and `uuid.bytes_le` — little-endian is the one that hits). **Run `make check-mdl` before pushing any new `mdl-examples/` file**: CI runs every example as a POSITIVE test unless it is named `*.fail.mdl`, so a fixture demonstrating a refusal fails the build. Split it — refused statements in the `.fail.mdl`, working forms in a sibling `.mdl`, each pointing at the other — so both halves are actually gated rather than only the negative one. ako/mxcli-captrack

raw: | `mxcli check --references` refuses a page mxbuild builds, with "microflow data source M.F has no argument for parameter 'P' … does not fill it in, even when an object of the right type is in scope" (CE1571) | `mdl/executor/validate_datasource_args.go` | The rule was generalised from a sound measurement to a false one. A page **parameter** of the parameter's type does not auto-map (measured, still true); an enclosing **data context** of a compatible type **does**. The two are different things and the message asserted the wrong one as fact. Re-measured on mxbuild 11.13.0, five widgets in one `mx check`: nested in a dataview of the parameter's type → **no error**; matching context two levels up with a mismatched dataview between → **no error**; mismatched context → CE1571; no context → CE1571; page parameter of the exact type → CE1571. The walk now carries a `dataContext` (the entity types of the enclosing data containers), resolved from the container's data source — a flow's **return** type, a `database` source's entity, a `parameter` source's page-parameter type. An **association** or **selection** source marks the context *unresolved*, which **suppresses** the report: guessing wrong in that direction is exactly what rejected the working page. A **primitive** parameter is always reported (a data context can never supply a String), which is what keeps the rule sharp. The three rejected shapes are the controls — without them the fix is indistinguishable from deleting the rule. Generalisation is delegated to `entityCompatibility`, which accepts a relation in **either** direction: a missed CE1571 costs a build error mxbuild still catches, a wrong refusal costs a working page. |

| `mxcli check` warns MDL071 "attribute 'Year' is an OQL reserved word — … a view entity referencing it unquoted fails to build with CE0174" on a **non-persistent** entity | `mdl/executor/validate_oql_reserved_names.go`, `mdl/executor/cmd_enumerations.go` | The warning's premise cannot arise: an NPE has no table. Measured rather than reasoned about, by pointing a view entity at one — mxbuild 11.13.0 refuses the **reference**, not the name: `CE0174 "Entity 'X' cannot be used in OQL, because it is a non-persistable entity"`. `oqlUnreachable` skips a **known** non-persistent entity, for both the attribute name and the entity's own name. Persistence had to become **three-valued** (`entityPersistence`): `ALTER ENTITY … ADD ATTRIBUTE` carries no kind, and the two rules keyed on it want opposite defaults for "unknown" — MDL020 stays silent unless known persistent, MDL071 stays loud unless known non-persistent. The old boolean passed `false` for ALTER meaning *unknown*, so a naive gate on it would have silently dropped MDL071 from the path where a name lands on an entity that already has references. VIEW and EXTERNAL entities count as reachable — a view entity's own attribute name **is** its select alias, the one MDL071 case that genuinely needs a rename. |

| `mxcli check … --references` reports "nanoflow not found: Mod.Flow" for a nanoflow created **earlier in the same script**, printed directly under the line "(Note: References to objects created within the script are skipped)". `exec` runs the same file without complaint and `mx check` is 0 errors | `mdl/executor/helpers.go` (`validateWidgetReferences`) | One omission in a list of five. The function consults `sc.<kind>` — the same-script exemption — for microflows, pages, snippets and entities, and for **nanoflows alone** it did not, so every widget reference kind was exempt except that one. Fix is `&& !sc.nanoflows[ref]`, matching its four siblings. Note this is the **inverse** of MDL-ORDER01, which exists to catch a reference to something created *later*; a rule pair like that is worth checking in both directions when one half is added. The test asserts all the kinds in one table so the omission cannot reappear on a different line, and the control is a nanoflow in neither the project nor the script, which must still be reported. Reported as ledger #138; example `mdl-examples/bug-tests/ledger-138-snippet-nanoflow-same-script.mdl` |

symptom: `mxcli check --references` and `exec` both pass, then the native `mx check` fails **CE6681** "It is not possible to jump to end activities or jump-to activities" on a workflow `jump to`
cause: `buildJumpTo` set the jump activity's **`Name` to its target's name**. Mendix resolves `TargetActivity` **by name**, so the jump could resolve to itself — and CE6681 then describes a different fault than the real one (an unresolved target, or a stolen name)
insight: **A jump target is the only INTRA-document reference a workflow has, and nothing resolved it** — `validateWorkflowStatementRefs` covers external refs (microflows, pages, entities) and returns before looking at activity names. Two defects, and the second is not in the report: naming the jump after its target also breaks a **forward** jump to a *valid* activity, because deduplication renames the SECOND activity carrying a name — measured, `jump ... then StepB` gives the jump `StepB` and the real target `StepB2`. The reported "works" row of the trigger table holds only for a backward jump, which is why loops looked fine. So fixing only the unresolved case would have left the other half. Fix both ends: give the jump its own name (`JumpTo`, deduped) so it can never collide, **and** run deduplication in two passes with jumps LAST so a jump never claims a name a real activity wanted. Wire the rule into `ValidateWorkflow` **and** call the same function from `execCreateWorkflow` (the #833 lesson — exec is reachable without check). Compute the valid-target set by running the real builders over the AST rather than re-deriving names: a `call microflow M.SUB_X` activity is named `SUB_X`, and a second copy of that rule would drift into false refusals. List the valid names in the suggestion — they are not visible in the script, which is most of why the wrong one is easy to reach. Exclude jumps from the target set (CE6681 again). Two traps hit while doing it: a nested `if jumpPass { if !jumpPass {` from a careless bulk edit silently disabled all jump renaming (caught only by a two-jump uniqueness test — CE0495 would have been the next report), and `Inner` is an MDL keyword, so a test fixture using it fails to parse for reasons unrelated to the fix. mendixlabs/mxcli#1005

symptom: `DESCRIBE WORKFLOW` output fails `mxcli check` — `mismatched input '[%UserRole_Banker%]' expecting ';'` on a `targeting users xpath` line, and every later statement cascades
cause: The emitter wrote `fmt.Sprintf("… '%s'", v)` — quotes in the format string, escaping (if any) at the call site. **6 of 23 emit sites did not escape**: both xpath variants, the user-task caption, the workflow-level due date, and both outcome values
insight: **Return the quotes WITH the escaping** — `mdlQuoted(s)` yields `'…''…'` complete, so an unescaped emit cannot be written by omission. Escaping at the call site is one thing to remember per site, and the count of sites only grows. Assert the emitted MDL **parses** (wrap the fragment in a minimal `create workflow … end workflow;` and run `visitor.Build`), never that it contains a particular escape — a substring assertion encodes the very escape under test, so it passes for the wrong reason. Route the harness through `formatWorkflowActivities`, not the per-activity formatter: the statement terminator is appended by the caller, so calling the formatter directly produces unparseable output for reasons unrelated to the bug. Emit tests only cover positions the test constructs, so add a **source scan** for a literal `'%s'` in the describers — the real failure mode is a *new* site added later, and `mdlQuoted` carrying its own quotes is what makes that scan sound. The reported symptom was the XPath (its payload is full of quoted constraints, so *every* XPath-targeted user task hits it); the caption one needs only an apostrophe — `Manager's review`. mendixlabs/mxcli#1006

symptom: `DESCRIBE WORKFLOW` output is refused by `mxcli check` with **MDL-WF04** — "a standalone `annotation` … produces a model Mendix cannot load"; 13 errors from one unmodified describe of a 23-activity workflow
cause: The describer emitted `annotation '<text>';` — the exact construct MDL-WF04 exists to refuse, and that `execCreateWorkflow` refuses again. Two parts of the tree disagreed **in comments**: the emitter said "emitted as a parseable MDL statement so it survives round-trips", the validator said it cannot be loaded. The emitter's comment was the stale one
insight: **When a describer and a validator disagree, one of them has a stale comment — read both before choosing a side.** The reporter framed these as canvas annotations; they are not. `formatAnnotation` is called at 10 sites, always with an activity's **attached** `Annotation`, and describe converted attached → standalone, which is the refused form. That distinction changes the fix: the issue's "support writing annotations" needs a grammar change, because `MDLWorkflow.g4` has only the standalone `workflowAnnotationStmt` — **no MDL input can express an attached annotation today**, even though the write path stores one. So a comment loses nothing that was reachable. Note the asymmetry that caused this: the **microflow** domain has `@annotation 'text'` as an activity prefix and round-trips it properly; giving workflow activities the same prefix is the non-lossy fix, and is a feature, not this bug. Two traps: a `--` comment runs to end of line, so a multi-line annotation must be prefixed **per line** or the tail becomes stray tokens (the same failure the statement form had), and the standalone branch must set `isComment` or the terminator logic appends `;` to a comment. Assert the emitted MDL **parses AND passes ValidateWorkflow AND still contains the text** — checking only that the keyword is gone also passes for an emit that dropped the annotation entirely. mendixlabs/mxcli#1007

raw: | Every `IMAGE` widget mxcli authors on Mendix 11.13 fails `mx check` with **CE0463** "the definition of this widget has changed", including the exact `pluggablewidget` form an existing bug-test documents as fixed. `mxcli fix widgets` clears it | `mdl/executor/widget_engine.go` (`hiddenUnnamedProperties`, the mapping loop) | **Case B**, established before any hypothesis (diagnose-ce0463 Step 0): the baseline blank project ships **10 Studio Pro-authored widgets of the same widget id** and reports **0** CE0463; one mxcli-authored Image makes it 1. So the tool is the variable — and those 10 are a known-good reference in the same project, better than a template extraction. The exhaustive path diff came back with **every path present on both sides** and four differing values, two of them content; the `Type` (PropertyTypes schema) subtree and the `TypePointer`→`PropertyKey` mapping were identical. **Two hypotheses tested and falsified, which is why they are recorded**: (a) *key order* — mxcli's node is not in the reference's alphabetical order, a documented CE0463 cause, but the same page's mxcli-authored Datagrid and Badge share that order and pass; (b) *the width value* — authoring `Width: 48` explicitly passes, so 48 is not rejected. The cause is the interaction: the widget **hides `width` when `widthUnit` is "auto"**, and a hidden property must hold its DECLARED default. The engine *skipped* the mapping for a hidden property, which leaves the widget **template's captured value** — image.json holds 48 while its own `ValueType.DefaultValue` says 100. mxcli's own **MDL-WIDGET10** already said so verbatim ("a non-default value there fails the build with CE0463 (the default is \"100\")"), so `check` refused what `exec` emitted: the fix makes the writer read `widgetPropertyDefaults`, the checker's own source, so the two cannot disagree again. The engine's comment already stated the invariant correctly — "the hidden ones **at their default**, so hidden means default-valued, not absent" — and skipping only coincides with that when the template happens to be at the default. Where no default can be looked up (a datasource has none) it still skips, so #956's File Uploader pruning is unchanged. **Control**: stub the `SetPrimitive` and CE0463 returns end-to-end. Follow-on the fix *revealed* (CE0463 was masking it): the default `ImageType: image` needs an image-collection entry MDL cannot name, so the bare form builds to Mendix's own "No image selected." — now **MDL-WIDGET22** at check time, and it found the same breakage in four of the repo's own examples. Reported as mxcli-formula1 FINDINGS §69/§142 |

| An `image` widget mxcli wrote shows nothing, and `mx check` fails with **"No image selected."**; and a `describe` → rename → `exec` copy of an Atlas layout (or any page with a brand image) comes out with the image gone, describe having emitted `image staticImage1 (Responsive: false)` with no reference at all | `mdl/executor/widget_engine.go` (the `image` operation), `mdl/executor/widget_defs.go` + `mdl/executor/widget_registry.go` (`operationForType`, `defaultKnownOperations`), `mdl/backend/widgetobj/builder.go` (`SetImage`, `setImageValue`), `mdl/backend/mutation.go` + `mdl/backend/mcp/widget.go`, `{modelsdk,sdk}/widgets/definitions/image.def.json` (`imageObject` → `Image`), `mdl/executor/cmd_pages_describe_pluggable.go` (`extractCustomWidgetPropertyImage`) + `cmd_pages_describe_output.go` (`describeImageWidgetProps`) | MDL had no spelling for **which** image an image widget shows, so its default source (`ImageType: image`, an image collection entry) could never be satisfied and describe had nothing to emit — mxcli-formula1 FINDINGS §142. The name is three parts like an icon reference, `Module.Collection.Image`, stored as a plain string on the `WidgetValue`'s `Image` key. Both halves are needed: with only the write, a round trip still loses it. `setImageValue` **replaces** the existing `Image` key and never adds one — adding a key the widget definition does not declare is the CE0463 shape. Controls: stub `setImageValue` → `TestSetImageValue_SetsTheQualifiedName` fails; stub the describe emission → `TestDescribeImageWidget_EmitsTheImageReference` fails |

| `image imgTypo (Image: 'MyFirstModule.Images.NoSuchImage')` passes `mxcli check --references` ("Check passed!") and the build then fails **CE1613** "The selected image '…' no longer exists." | `mdl/executor/validate_widget_image_ref.go` (new, `imageRefErrors`, `buildImageQualifiedNames`), `mdl/executor/helpers.go` (`widgetRefCollector.images`, `validateWidgetReferences`) | Wiring `Image:` created a new qualified name and nothing resolved it — every other name a widget carries (microflow, nanoflow, page, snippet, entity) already was. This one has **three** parts, so the two mistakes get two messages: a missing collection sends the reader to `show image collections`, a missing image to that collection's contents (which the diagnostic lists). A **nil** name set means the collections could not be read and nothing is reported; an empty non-nil one is a real answer. No same-script exemption — MDL cannot create an image collection entry, so the reference can only resolve against the project. Control: `TestImageRefErrors_KnownImageIsClean`, and `TestImageRefErrors_NoCollectionsMeansNoOpinion` for the failed-read direction |

symptom: `main` goes red on a test that passed in **both** PRs that touched it — here `TestDescribeWorkflow_NoAnnotationEmitsNoComment`: `unexpected violations [MDL-WF05] for a plain jump`
cause: Two PRs merged in sequence. One added a validator rule (MDL-WF05, dangling `jump to` target); the other's control test asserted `len(violations) == 0` over a fixture that was **not a valid workflow** — a lone jump whose target did not exist. Each CI run was green because neither saw the other's change
insight: **A test fixture that is not a valid instance of the thing under test is a landmine for the next rule.** "No violations at all" is only meaningful over input that *should* have none; over an invalid fixture it silently asserts "no rule has been written yet that notices this". Fix the **fixture**, not the rule. Generalise: when a test asserts the ABSENCE of diagnostics, make the input something you would be happy to ship. Two green PRs can still merge to red and **neither PR's CI can detect it** — the only protection is a fixture that does not depend on which rules exist today. Found by running `make test` on an unrelated docs branch cut from the merged main, which is an argument for doing that on any branch cut after a batch merge.

symptom: `filter($L, Amount > 0)` — or any FILTER/FIND predicate with a bare attribute and an operator other than `=` — fails the build with CE0117 "Error(s) in expression.", while the same attribute with `=` builds fine. `mxcli check` and `check --references` both pass. Reported as a Mendix 11.13 regression.
cause: The unfinished half of bug #343. Mendix has two filter operations: `Microflows$Filter` takes a member NAME (filter by attribute) and `Microflows$FilterByExpression` takes an expression evaluated per item with the item bound to `$currentObject`. #343 rerouted only `attr = value` to the by-attribute form; every other predicate still fell through to the expression form, where mxcli stored the authored text verbatim — and a bare attribute is not a valid Mendix expression. So the split was on the OPERATOR and invisible to the author: `Status = 'x'` built, `Status != 'x'` did not.
insight: Rewrite a bare name that PROVABLY resolves to a member of the list's element entity into `$currentObject/<member>`; refuse one that does not resolve (it used to surface as CE0117 at build time); pass through untouched when the element entity cannot be determined, which proves nothing either way. An association takes its module qualifier in the path, an attribute does not. The predicate is a frozen `SourceExpr` (`buildSourceExpression` in the visitor), so the rewrite has to patch the source TEXT, skipping single-quoted literals — `filter($L, Qty > 0 and Status != 'Amount')` must not rewrite the `'Amount'` inside the literal. Do not blame the Mendix version without running both: the issue reported "reproduces on 11.13.0, not 11.11.0" and the identical 7-error probe on mxbuild 11.11.0 and 11.13.0 disproves it — the fork is in mxcli, and nothing in it depends on the version. `mx check -j <file>` is the attribution tool: the console output names only the activity ("List operation activity 'Filter by expression'"), so two errors on one line read as one microflow; the JSON carries `document-name` per location. MDL-LISTOP01 keys on scope, not on the name — `$item` is valid in a predicate when it is the enclosing loop's iterator, which is exactly how CLAUDE.md's O(N) `find` idiom is written, so flagging the name would break the documented pattern. Control for the whole fix: stub `qualifyIteratorAttributes` to return the condition unchanged and the repro goes 0 → 7 x CE0117 with the two `=` cases staying green, which is also the #343 regression guard.

symptom: A copied Atlas layout (or any page mxcli authors) fails `mx check` with **CE0463** on its Image widget, and a full field-level diff against Studio Pro's own widget differs in exactly **one line of 1480** — `maxHeight`, mxcli's `0` against the installed package's declared default
cause: Same class as the §69 width/height fix, which did not cover it — and why is the point. The reset was applied in a loop over the definition's **property mappings**, and a mapping is what gives a property an MDL keyword: `width`/`height` have one, `maxHeight` has none, so it was never visited and the widget TEMPLATE's captured value stood. Two further halves, each independently load-bearing (stub either and the test fails): a rule whose CONDITION is an unmapped property (`maxHeight` is hidden when `maxHeightUnit` = "none") was always indeterminable so never fired — the declared default is the right fallback there, because nothing can have moved an unnamable property off it; and `def.PropertyVisibility` is **empty** for every widget whose rules are lifted live from the `.mpk`, which is most of them, so a lookup keyed on that field silently finds nothing (both consumers now share `visibilityRules()`).
insight: The general rule: **the set of properties that must be default-valued is the widget's editorConfig to decide, not mxcli's** — making it a subset of what MDL has words for was the mistake. The third trap was found only end-to-end; the unit test passed while the command still wrote the wrong value. Control, end-to-end on a real 11.13 project with the Image `.mpk` patched to declare `maxHeight` 250 (the 1.6.0 value the finding measured, since that version was not obtainable): pre-fix binary writes 0 and all four mxcli-authored Images fail CE0463; fixed binary writes 250 and all four are clean, while `minHeight` stays at its own declared 0 — per-property from the package, not a blanket value. The project's ~60 Studio Pro-authored Images stay stale under both, which is the package change itself and not mxcli: the Step 0 discrimination diagnose-ce0463.md asks for. Reported as mxcli-ledger FINDINGS §142.
